# Concordance to the Quran in Western Apache

**Robert Tilford — Ayah Companion**
**DRAFT — NOT PUBLISHED**

## Introduction

A concordance is an index of words. For every distinct word form that
stands in *The Quran in Western Apache*, this book gives the form, the
ground it stands on, and a complete list of the verses where it occurs,
so that a reader who meets a word anywhere in the translation can find
every other place it stands, and a reader who doubts a word can trace
it back to the published record it came from. It is the companion of
the translation itself and of the glossary that shelves beside it: the
glossary says what a word means and where it was found; the concordance
says everywhere the word is used.

**What it was built from.** The concordance was counted mechanically
from the landed manuscript exactly as it stands today, 2026-11-24 —
all 6,236 verses, including the last three seats closed this morning
by Robert Tilford's rulings: the description built from the Western
Apache New Testament's own frame at Acts 16:16, seated at 52:29 and
69:42 for the soothsayer (its forms — *ch'iidn*, *biyi'*,
*golį́į́go*, *o'įįń* — are indexed here like every other form, at those
verses among their other seats), and the two disclosed English
stand-ins at 2:61, which are listed separately at the end of this book
and marked as what they are. The citations rest on the lane's own
receipted grounding data only: the build glossary and the New
Testament corpus forms table. No outside source was consulted, no form
was added, and the manuscript itself was not touched.

**How an entry reads.** Each entry gives the form in bold, then how
many times it occurs and in how many verses, then its ground, then the
full list of its verses in order. A verse marked (×2) or (×3) holds
the form that many times. Forms are grouped under their lowercase
headword: capital letters at the heads of sentences are positional in
this orthography, so a form printed with a capital where a sentence
begins is counted under the same headword as its lowercase self. The
manuscript prints two shapes of the letter n — ṉ and ń — in different
places; they are kept as printed and never merged. Apostrophes inside
a word are part of the form and are kept. An apostrophe at the very
edge of a word in the manuscript — a closing quotation mark, or an
edge glottal — is not carried into the headword: headwords follow the
citation shapes of the lane's own record, the New Testament corpus
forms table and the glossary, which print, for example, *ałdó*,
*ła*, *bich'į* and *biyi* without an edge apostrophe, and the
citations in this book verify against those shapes. The entries are
alphabetised by the Western Apache alphabet, in which ch, dl, dz, gh,
kw, nd, nt, nz, sh, tł, ts and zh count as single letters; a small
number of carried names and loanwords (such as *ramadan* and
*pomegranates*) stand under their own letters as printed. The book's
unnumbered Basmalah opening lines repeat verse 1:1 and are not indexed
separately.

**The ground under each entry, stated in tiers.** Not every form in
the translation is receipted in the same way, and this book says which
is which rather than dressing them alike. Of the 2,238
headwords: 808 stand on a direct receipt — the form is the
headword form of a glossary entry, or it stands exactly in the New
Testament corpus forms table, or both. 44 occur inside a
receipted glossary phrase. 101 stand in the corpus or the
glossary under a variant accent spelling, and the entry names the
spelling held. 714 are built on a receipted stem, and the entry
names the stem and its ground. 35 are mentioned in the build
record in the glossary's own notes, and the entry points to the note.
And 536 headwords, carrying 4,869 of the book's
134,126 indexed occurrences — about one occurrence
in 28 — have no receipt for their exact form in the grounding
files the lane holds. That figure is reported here, not smoothed over: the build
receipted its vocabulary at the level of glossary entries and corpus
forms, and many seated forms are inflections and fixed narrative forms
whose exact surface shape was not separately receipted. Their entries
say so in plain words.

**The count, reconciled.** The manuscript's numbered verses hold
134,890 word tokens. From these,
110 tokens are the ruled inline
help-flag at 2:69 — an editorial note standing in the text by Robert
Tilford's ruling, apparatus rather than translation, and not indexed
here — and 652 tokens are
punctuation standing alone, which index nothing. The two English
stand-ins at 2:61 are listed separately, as said. The remaining
134,126 occurrences are indexed below, under
2,238 headwords (2,789
distinct forms as printed, capitals included), and the entries'
occurrence counts sum to exactly 134,126 — the
arithmetic closes.

**Status.** This concordance was prepared with the help of artificial
intelligence, under Robert Tilford's direction, from his finished
translation. Like the translation, it is machine-assisted work by
non-speakers of Western Apache, and it is not speaker-reviewed. It is
offered freely, as the translation is: free to read and free to
download, never sold, attribution requested.
